summary: NVIDIA Omniverse NuRec is the company's neural reconstruction and rendering stack for physical-AI simulation, and it is scored here together with 3DGRUT, the Apache-2.0 research code that trains the scenes and exports them. Real camera and lidar recordings go in through NCore, NVIDIA's documented multi-sensor data specification with its own pose graph, metric conventions and converters for the public driving datasets; a reconstruction comes out as a USD package that separates the static background from moving objects, carries a driveable road map, rig trajectories and the trained checkpoint, and is rendered by gsplat inside Isaac Sim or another simulator. Two things put this subject at the centre of the capture question for a standards group. First, splats have reached OpenUSD as a schema rather than as a private payload: Omniverse publishes these environments as USD stages using ParticleField geometry that the renderer draws natively alongside ordinary polygons, and NVIDIA is deprecating its own custom NuRec package in favour of that standard schema. Second, this is the only capture subject scored anywhere on the map that treats time as first-class — moving objects are separated into their own layers with tracks and trajectories — because the customer is a robot that has to drive through the scene. Everything here needs NVIDIA hardware, and much of it needs a container from NVIDIA's own registry; nothing here runs on a phone.

coverage.note: Rasterisation and ray tracing are both here and deliberately mixed: primary rays are rasterised and secondary rays traced, so reflections, refractions and shadows work on Gaussian content. There is still no general render graph in the reconstruction stack; the graph belongs to the simulator that receives the stage.
